name: LlamaIndex
subcategory: RAG / agent framework, now positioned as a document-processing platform (LlamaParse)
origin_detail: Begun by Jerry Liu as a side project in late 2022 and published to GitHub in November 2022 as GPT (Tree) Index (repo created 2022-11-02; first commit 'Add initial version of GPTIndex' 2022-11-06), later renamed LlamaIndex; Liu joined by former colleague Simon Suo; company formally incorporated 2023-04-01; HQ San Francisco
openness_notes: Initial 3: Nov 2022 to 2024 the product was the MIT-licensed GPT Index/LlamaIndex library and nothing proprietary was sold. Current 2 (open core): the framework stays MIT and the company keeps releasing open tools (LiteParse, Apache-2.0, Mar 2026), but the business is LlamaParse, which the pricing FAQ calls 'our commercial platform' (the new name for LlamaCloud; GA with the Mar 2025 Series A), sold by credits per parsed page with Pay-as-you-go, Pro ($500/month) and Enterprise tiers, and as SaaS, single-tenant, customer-cloud or on-prem. The GitHub repo now describes LlamaIndex as 'the document processing platform for AI', so the company's centre of gravity has moved from the open framework to a closed parsing/OCR product. No relicensing found.

license_history.note: Repo created 2022-11-02; initial GPTIndex commit 2022-11-06 included 'add license'; repo licence MIT as of 2026-11
General availability announced 2025-03-04 with the Series A; SOC 2 Type 2, EU region
Local, offline parser; repo created 2026-02-09, announced 2026-03-19; later Rust core with TS/Python bindings

risk_events: Repositioned from an open RAG framework to a proprietary document-processing platform; revenue depends on the closed LlamaParse product rather than the MIT framework
Small disclosed capital ($27.5M plus undisclosed minority stakes from Databricks and KPMG, May 2025) against much larger framework rivals (e.g., LangChain $460M by Nov 2026)
Single-vendor governance: no foundation for the framework
robustness: MIT framework with ~53k GitHub stars and 8.6k forks (Nov 2026) and 3M+ monthly downloads (Mar 2025) would survive the company; LiteParse is Apache-2.0. Commercial customers named include Rakuten, Carlyle, Salesforce, KPMG and Cemex; LlamaParse had processed 'hundreds of millions of documents' for 'tens of thousands' of users by Mar 2025. Strategic minority investors (Databricks, KPMG) add partners but no disclosed valuation.
physical_science_relevance: Moderate: parsing PDFs and building retrieval over documents is directly useful for scientific literature mining and lab-report search; LiteParse offers an offline, local parser, which suits labs with data-governance limits.
openness_effect_assessment: The open framework drove very fast adoption (16k stars and 200k monthly PyPI downloads within about six months, 3M+ monthly downloads by Mar 2025), which funded an $8.5M seed. Monetisation came from a separate proprietary product (LlamaParse/LlamaCloud), and the company still uses Apache-2.0 releases (LiteParse) as a funnel. Disclosed funding stayed modest ($27.5M), so openness bought distribution but not, on the evidence fetched, a large valuation.
key_takeaway: LlamaIndex followed LangChain's playbook (MIT framework, closed cloud product) without relicensing, but drifted furthest from its open roots: the repo now calls the project 'the document processing platform for AI' and the money is in credit-metered LlamaParse. With only $27.5M disclosed and no valuation found, it is evidence that permissive AI frameworks are a cheap distribution channel but that the business is the hosted, closed service.

notes: funding_total_usd $27.5M is the company-stated total at the Series A ($8.5M seed + $19M Series A); the Databricks and KPMG minority investments (2025-05-01) were undisclosed and are excluded.
No valuation, revenue or headcount was found on fetched pages; the blog index shows no later funding round through Nov 2026.
Wikipedia's LlamaIndex article carries a notice that it may have been edited for undisclosed payment; figures used here were cross-checked against LlamaIndex's own posts.
The commits API listing for LICENSE showed only two commits and no licence-type change; MIT is the current SPDX licence of the repo.
Wikipedia gives the original GitHub name as 'GPT Tree Index'; the first commit message says 'GPTIndex'.
